weights.comment: The ten-lever migration formula (FEAT-9995385616, Aaron 2026-11-18). levers: ten equal weights of 0.1 (must sum to 1 within 1e-6; equal is the data, not a code rule, so a balance pass is a data edit); one entry per lever, each named once. modifiers: safety and environment stay OUTSIDE the ten at full strength (0.1 each, same slope per point as the old seven-term formula), each its own panel line, each contributing weight x (value - A_world). reputation: the weight of the momentum / pride kick (0.15, unchanged). reinforcers: weights of the named momentum inputs (sports, welfare, education, prospects, wellpaidjobs, hospitals, parks) - inert today because none is built; each, once built, moves the momentum's target by weight x (value - A_world) (0.02 each is a directional placeholder). Balance pass pending (Aaron's balance-number regime, 2026-08-13).

built.comment: Which migration inputs count (BUG-1243). SHIPPED VALUES ARE TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR (both modifiers built), pending Aaron's choice between options A, B and C on BUG-1243; each option is a one-line edit here. built.modifiers.safety / .environment: true = the reading counts as weight x (reading - world.aWorld) points (today); false = the modifier is not built and adds exactly 0 points, the F5 panel reads 'not built yet' (option A, Aaron's ruling of 2026-11-18 before the early-game cost was measured: about 2 arrivals a month instead of 12). The reading is computed and stored either way. A flag missing from this block means built, so an older data file behaves as it always did. Unknown keys anywhere in this file are refused, so a misspelt switch cannot silently do nothing. The parks lever is NOT flagged here: its input is real (zoning entertainment opens a leisure venue), see leisure.floorAtBaseline and BUG-1245.

whenUnbuilt.comment: What a modifier flagged false (not built) contributes. neutral: exactly 0 points (option A). floorAtBaseline: option C, the modifier counts max(reading, world.aWorld), so it adds points when its reading is above the baseline and exactly 0 when below, never negative; the F5 panel shows it as built with the floored value. Only matters while the modifier's built flag is false. Option C = set both built flags false AND both of these to floorAtBaseline.

world.comment: The outside-world baseline A_world that every lever and modifier is measured against. 40 is today's value; valid range 0 to 100; a lower value gives a new city more arrivals (option B = built flags false plus a lower value, 20 or 0). A_world is re-read from this file on every load and is NOT stored in a save: a save made under one value and loaded under another continues under the new value, deterministically.

environment.comment: Directional placeholder (GR#15): total uncollected+disposal-backlog waste (kg, summed general+recycling+food) at which engine.attract's Environment term reads 50/100. Mirrors data/crime.json's safety.halfSaturationActiveCrime curve shape (see internal/engine/crime/api.go's SafetyTerm). Balance pass pending (Aaron's balance-number regime, 2026-08-13).

leisure.comment: Directional placeholder (GR#15): weekly patronage capacity (person-hours, engine.leisure's Venue.Capacity unit) assigned by the compose->leisure venue-registration bridge to every completed engine.build ZoneEntertainment order. engine.build's zone catalogue carries one generic 'entertainment' type today, with no venue-category sub-signal, so the bridge always opens one CategoryCommunity venue at this one capacity figure — a coarse composite, not a real per-building capacity read. Balance pass pending. floorAtBaseline (BUG-1245, off = today): when true the parks lever never reads below world.aWorld, so it adds 0 points before the first venue and a venue can only raise it.

jobAvailability.comment: Directional placeholder (GR#15, FEAT-167 completion): the engine.firms LabourMarket().VacancyRatePerMille value at which the JobAvailability term reads 50/100 (docs/planning/icd/engine.firms-labourmarket.md). VacancyRatePerMille carries no upper clamp (vacancies can exceed workforce), so a half-saturation curve — the same shape data/attract_terms.json's environment.pollutionHalfSaturationKg already uses — maps it onto attract's bounded [0,100] scale: term = 100 * rate / (rate + this). 100 per-mille (10% vacancy rate) reading 50/100 is a directional starting point, not a balance-passed figure. Baseline one wires no automatic firm-founding into the composition root (a separate, larger integration outside this ICD's scope), so TotalVacancies legitimately reads 0 — and this term 0 — until that lands; the formula is proven to move under a direct engine.firms mutation (see compose's servicesfirms_wire_test.go).

serviceCoverage.comment: Directional placeholder (GR#15, FEAT-167 completion): scales engine.services CoverageSummary().CoverageRatio (docs/planning/icd/engine.services-coverage.md) — already clamped to [0,1], or exactly 1.0 when city-wide TotalDemand is zero (coverage.go's coverageRatio) — onto attract's [0,100] term scale. 100 is the neutral (no-op) scale: term = 100 * CoverageRatio * (this/100). Baseline one wires no automatic engine.build -> engine.services registration bridge into the composition root (a separate, larger integration outside this ICD's scope — the ICD's own open decision 1), so CoverageRatio legitimately reads the zero-demand default (1.0, term 100) until that bridge lands; the formula is proven to move under a direct engine.services mutation (see compose's servicesfirms_wire_test.go).
